params.name: age_hr_reserve_gate

payload.simplified: 3195 always active on data (thal:7 in {-0.769,1.300} => 3195 in {0.155,2.376}); exact affine reduction: 1718 = relu(-1.518 - 1.490 age + 1.024 thalach - 1.535 thal:7). Pre-activation bias is -0.337 without reversible defect and -3.514 with it.

records.narrative: Closed form; relay 3195 is affine on the data so the gate is a single ReLU of age, thalach and thal:7.

payload.outcome: disease rate 11.3% when gate active vs 60.5% when inactive
payload.ablation: removing the 1718 readout lowers train AUC 0.9434 -> 0.9378 (largest single nonlinear term); readout logit SD 0.64
payload.activity: 1718 active 33.1% overall; 50.7% of the 152 patients without reversible defect (thal:7=0) vs 3.3% of the 90 with it

records.narrative: Gate is a protective 'good heart-rate reserve for age, no reversible defect' detector.

params.hypothesis: Heart-rate-reserve gate 1718 = ReLU(-0.812 - 1.490*age + 1.024*thalach - 0.762*thal:7 - 0.720*R3195), with relay R3195 = ReLU(0.981 + 1.073*thal:7). Hypothesis: 3195 is an always-on affine relay of thal:7 (thal:7 is one-hot, z-scored to {-0.769, 1.300}, so 3195 in {0.155, 2.376} > 0), which makes the gate's net thal:7 coefficient -1.535 and bias -1.518. The gate fires for patients whose achieved max heart rate is high for their age (thalach up, age down) AND who do NOT have a reversible thallium defect; its readout into the output is -0.582, so it is a protective (risk-lowering) term. EVIDENCE (train, n=242): 3195 is active for 100% of patients, so the gate reduces exactly to 1718 = ReLU(-1.518 - 1.490*age + 1.024*thalach - 1.535*thal:7). Active 33% overall: 51% of patients without a reversible defect vs 3% with one. Disease rate 11% when active vs 60% when inactive. Mean |sensitivity|: age 0.49 > thalach 0.34 > thal:7 (two copies) 0.25 each. Removing its readout drops train AUC 0.943 -> 0.938, the largest single nonlinear effect (readout logit SD 0.64). Supported.

params.name: st_slope_chol_gate

payload.simplified: 3464 active 92.6% (zero only for z-chol < -1.29); where active, 1476 = relu(-0.229 + 0.770 oldpeak + 1.145 slope:2 - 0.378 chol). slope:2 in {-0.913, 1.095} so slope:2 shifts the pre-activation by 2.30 between categories.

records.narrative: Closed form; the chol relay is near-affine.

payload.outcome: disease rate 66.7% when active vs 23.2% when inactive; corr(1476, oldpeak)=0.69
payload.ablation: removing the 1476 readout lowers train AUC 0.9434 -> 0.9418; readout logit SD 0.18
payload.activity: 1476 active 48.3%; 98.2% of the 110 flat-slope (slope:2) patients vs 6.8% of the others

records.narrative: Gate is essentially a flat-ST-slope indicator whose magnitude grows with ST depression and shrinks with cholesterol.

params.hypothesis: Flat-ST-slope gate 1476 = ReLU(0.257 + 1.145*slope:2 + 0.770*oldpeak - 0.374*C3464), with C3464 = ReLU(1.300 + 1.011*chol). Hypothesis: a one-sided risk detector that opens for patients with a flat peak-exercise ST segment (slope:2), its height scaled by ST depression (oldpeak) and reduced by cholesterol via an almost-always-active affine chol relay (3464 is zero only when z-chol < -1.29). Readout into output +0.225 (raises risk). EVIDENCE (train, n=242): 3464 is active for 93% (off only when z-chol < -1.29), so 1476 is nearly ReLU(-0.229 + 1.145*slope:2 + 0.770*oldpeak - 0.378*chol). Active for 98% of the 110 flat-slope patients vs 7% of the others, so it acts as a flat-slope indicator whose height rises with oldpeak (corr 0.69) and falls with cholesterol. Disease rate 67% when active vs 23% when inactive. Mean |sensitivity|: slope:2 0.55 > oldpeak 0.37 > chol 0.17. Removing its readout drops train AUC 0.943 -> 0.942 (logit SD 0.18). Supported. The negative chol term partly offsets chol's direct +0.613 edge for flat-slope patients; no clinical reading is offered for that.

params.name: oldpeak_hinges

payload.readout: logit += 0.377*1946 + 0.411*3284: slope 0 below -0.218, 0.289 between kinks, 0.605 above 0.539 (per z-unit oldpeak)

records.narrative: Closed form of the hinge pair; a convex piecewise-linear function of oldpeak.

payload.activity: 1946 active 50% (121 patients, disease rate 63.6%); 3284 active 24% (58 patients, disease rate 79.3%)

records.narrative: Hinges confirmed: oldpeak raises risk only above about the median, and more steeply at high values.

params.hypothesis: Oldpeak hinge pair: 1946 = ReLU(0.167 + 0.767*oldpeak) and 3284 = ReLU(-0.582 + 1.003*1946). Hypothesis: a convex piecewise-linear function of ST depression alone, with kinks at z-oldpeak = -0.218 (1946 opens) and 0.539 (3284 opens). Both exits read out positively (0.377 and 0.411), so beyond the second kink the logit slope in oldpeak roughly doubles: mild ST depression adds a little risk, marked ST depression adds much more. EVIDENCE (train, n=242): 1946 active 50% (disease rate 64%), 3284 active 24% (disease rate 79%). Contribution to the logit 0.377*1946 + 0.411*3284 has slope 0 below z-oldpeak -0.218, 0.289 between the kinks and 0.605 above 0.539. Mean |sensitivity| to oldpeak: 0.38 for 1946, 0.18 for 3284. Removing either readout changes train AUC by <= 0.001. Supported: a small convex ST-depression dose-response.

params.name: heart_disease_logit

payload.note: from get_formula force=true latex_collapsed; the tool renders the output as relu(z), but for binary classification the evaluator applies sigmoid: p = sigmoid(z). Confirmed locally: sigmoid(z) reproduces compute_performance train AUC 0.9434 / acc 0.884 exactly.
payload.latex: z = -0.21 + 1.68 x_{ca} + 0.993 x_{cp:4} - 0.745 x_{sex:0} + 0.613 x_{chol_a} + 0.494 x_{slope:2_a} - 0.473 x_{slope:1} + 0.469 x_{trestbps} + 0.45 x_{sex:1} + 0.416 x_{cp:2} - 0.306 x_{fbs:1} + 0.288 x_{thal:7_a} + 0.282 x_{exang:1} - 0.279 x_{thal:6} - 0.179 x_{cp:1} - 0.0959 x_{thalach_a} + 0.0703 x_{restecg:1} - 0.582\,\mathrm{age\_hr\_reserve\_gate} + 0.225\,\mathrm{st\_slope\_chol\_gate} + 0.377\,\mathrm{oldpeak\_hinges}_0 + 0.411\,\mathrm{oldpeak\_hinges}_1

records.narrative: Root closed form: additive logit of linear core plus three child readouts.
Full coverage with 5 input splits; the explained network computes the same function.

payload.method: local logit decomposition z = linear core + sum(readout weight * node activation), readouts removed without re-fitting

records.narrative: Linear core carries most of the signal; the nonlinear children add +0.013 train AUC, mostly via the heart-rate-reserve gate.
Top drivers are direct-edge features; oldpeak (gate-only) ranks 10th and age (gate-only) 0.013.

params.hypothesis: Root: logit z = -0.210 + LINEAR CORE - 0.582*age_hr_reserve_gate + 0.225*st_slope_chol_gate + 0.377*oldpeak_hinges[1946] + 0.411*oldpeak_hinges[3284]; prediction = sigmoid(z) (the genome output node is shown as ReLU, but for binary classification the evaluator applies a sigmoid, so z is a logistic score). LINEAR CORE (16 direct input->output edges, z-scored inputs): ca +1.68, cp:4 +0.99, sex:0 -0.74, chol +0.61, slope:2 +0.49, slope:1 -0.47, trestbps +0.47, sex:1 +0.45, cp:2 +0.42, fbs:1 -0.31, thal:7 +0.29, exang:1 +0.28, thal:6 -0.28, cp:1 -0.18, thalach -0.10, restecg:1 +0.07. The signs mostly match cardiology: more fluoroscopy-coloured vessels (ca), asymptomatic chest pain (cp:4), male sex, higher cholesterol and resting BP, flat ST slope and exertional angina raise risk, and upsloping ST (slope:1) lowers it. Exceptions are cp:2 +0.42 and fbs:1 -0.31, which run against the usual clinical direction and are left unexplained. Eight inputs are unused (cp:3, fbs:0, restecg:0, restecg:2, exang:0, slope:3, thal:3, thal:4). Age and oldpeak have no direct edge: they act only through the gates. COMPOSITION: purely additive in the logit. The three children add three nonlinear corrections to the linear core: (1) age_hr_reserve_gate, a protective ReLU that is on when max heart rate is high for the patient's age and there is no reversible thallium defect; (2) st_slope_chol_gate, a flat-ST-slope detector scaled up by oldpeak and down by cholesterol; (3) oldpeak_hinges, a convex two-kink dose-response in ST depression. The children share no hidden nodes. They are coupled only through shared input features (thal:7, thalach, chol and slope:2 also have direct edges, and oldpeak feeds both (2) and (3)). EVIDENCE (train, n=242): full model AUC 0.943, acc 0.884 (sigmoid(z) reproduces the evaluator exactly). Linear core alone gives AUC 0.930, so the nonlinear children add +0.013. Logit SD is 3.28 for the linear core vs 0.91 for all nonlinear readouts. Removing one readout at a time: 1718 -0.0057, 1476 -0.0017, 1946 -0.0007, 3284 -0.0004 AUC; all oldpeak-driven terms together -0.0064. Top SHAP features: ca, cp:4, sex:0, slope:2, slope:1 (all with direct edges). Interpretation: close to logistic regression, plus a protective heart-rate-reserve-for-age gate (blocked by a reversible defect) and two oldpeak/flat-slope ischaemia corrections.
